disclaimer: Estimation ratios compiled and cross-verified from public sold-data sources (June 2026). Every estimate links to live comps in-app — comps beat ratios.

gradeRatios.japaneseNote: Japanese modern cards have a compressed grade curve: PSA 9 ≈ 0.65 of PSA 10 (vs 0.45 English) and PSA 10 ≈ 1.6x raw (vs 2-5x English), because JPN gem rates run 60-70% vs 40-50% for English. JPN vintage behaves like English WOTC with steep ratios (est.). Separately, modern JPN cards carry a 15-40% absolute price premium over English equivalents — a price-level effect, not a grade-ratio effect. Caveats: the mid-era (2004-2019) band is interpolated, and all psa10OfRaw multipliers except modern English (verified 2-5x) are derived (est.). Modern PSA 8 sells at-or-below raw NM (0.8-1.0x raw) — flag negative grading EV. Chase/low-pop cards sit at the LOW end of every PSA 9/8 ratio range.

modernJa._note: Derived from verified JPN gem-rate research (est.): compressed grade curve, JPN modern PSA10 ~1.6x raw.

serviceDeltas.note: Typical equal-grade blend: CGC 10 Gem Mint ≈ 85% of PSA 10 on modern (gap narrowing to 90-95% on hot 2026 modern), ≈ 73% on vintage; CGC 9 ≈ 80% of PSA 9 (est.). CGC Pristine 10 is a SEPARATE tier above Gem Mint and the only CGC grade that reliably beats PSA 10 (~120%, range 100-200%) — never conflate Pristine with a plain CGC 10. Legacy pre-2023 CGC 9.5 ≈ today's CGC 10 and roughly matches PSA 9 money.

TAG 10 ≈ 67% of PSA 10 on modern, ≈ 57% on vintage — PSA commands a 35-60% premium over TAG and the gap widens on vintage/high-value cards (verified comps: 151 Charizard ex $185-220 PSA vs $115-135 TAG; Base Charizard $4,500-6,000+ vs $2,500-3,500). Lower TAG grades ≈ 60-70% of same-grade PSA (est., extrapolated).

BGS 9.5 ≈ 85% of a PSA 10 (the market's standard comparison; strong subgrades approach parity); PSA 10s resell 10-20% over equivalent BGS 9.5s. BGS 10 Pristine (non-black) ≈ 110% of PSA 10 (est., range 90-150%); BGS Black Label 10 ≈ 250% of PSA 10 (est.) — verified at 3-5x a regular BGS 10.

popIntel.claimVerdict: TRUE as a tendency, with a major caveat: a high PSA-10 population reliably COMPRESSES the grade premium (PSA 10 over raw/PSA 9) — but population is a modifier, not a deterministic price function. Pop-report inflation is self-reinforcing (price rises pull more raw copies into grading, raising pop and pushing the 10 back down), yet iconic/character-anchored cards can appreciate even at extreme pop: Van Gogh Pikachu has 40,000+ PSA 10s and still traded at ~$1,100-2,000 in 2025. High pop should trigger a warning, never an automatic 'grading not worth it.' Gem rate (<10% = hard to grade, >35% = easy) is more predictive than raw pop for grading ROI.
evidence: Umbreon VMAX Alt Art (Evolving Skies): ~3,000+ PSA 10s at a ~35% gem rate; PSA 10 prices declined ~30-40% as population expanded (est., PokemonPriceTracker figures)
McDonald's Pikachu JP M-P promo (2025): 273,159 graded / 239,939 PSA 10s — the saturation extreme (verified GemRate/Misprint counts)
Van Gogh Grey Felt Hat Pikachu (2023): ~105,000 graded / 40,000-46,800 PSA 10s, yet PSA 10s still sold ~$1,100-2,000 in 2025 — price and pop climbed together (the iconic override)
Charizard ex SIR 151 (2023): 90,861 graded / 26,443 PSA 10s; Eevee Prismatic Evolutions ETB promo (2025): 71,331 graded / 28,814 PSA 10s (verified counts)
Base Set Shadowless Charizard: ~486 PSA 10s, ~7.1% gem rate, only 3-4%/yr pop growth — values stable at ~$15k-25k
EX-era Gold Stars: typically <200 PSA 10s at 8-12% gem rates — appreciated 30-50%
Vintage pop is near-final (grade-able supply exhausted); modern (2020+) pop is still inflating fast, so discount today's modern pop and warn earlier (est.)

tiers.label: Low pop — scarcity premium intact
tiers.advice: PSA 10 premium runs 100-1000%+ over PSA 9 (est.); grading a clean raw copy is strongly favored.

tiers.label: Normal
tiers.advice: Premium ~50-200% over PSA 9 (est.); grading EV usually positive when the raw card clears grading cost (~$15-25/card all-in).

tiers.label: Elevated — premium compressing
tiers.advice: Premium compressing to ~20-50% over PSA 9 (est.); show AMBER warning and defer to live PSA 10 vs PSA 9/raw comps before grading.

tiers.label: High — commodity-grade
tiers.advice: Premium thins below ~20% (est.); grading rarely worth it on modern unless the card is an iconic/chase or gem rate is under 10%.

tiers.label: Saturated
tiers.advice: Grade premium mostly arbitraged away; skip grading unless iconic-override applies (Van Gogh Pikachu held $1k+ at 40k pop) — demand can outrun even extreme supply (est.).

popIntel.heuristic: Compute premium = PSA10_value - raw_value - grading_cost(~$20). RED ('likely not worth grading'): raw < ~$30 AND PSA10 pop > 5,000 AND era = modern (2020+) AND gem rate unknown or > 25%. AMBER ('premium compressing, check comps'): pop 1,000-5,000, OR modern with gem rate > 30%, OR raw value < grading cost regardless of pop. GREEN ('scarcity supports grading'): pop < 1,000 OR gem rate < 10% OR vintage with stable pop. Two overrides: (1) iconic/chase cards (Charizard, Pikachu, named promos, alt-art SIR/SAR) downgrade RED to AMBER; (2) live PSA10-vs-raw/PSA9 comps always beat the pop tier — pop is the prior, comps are the evidence. Gem rate = PSA10 pop / total graded; it beats raw pop as a predictor (est. thresholds, community consensus).

popUrlTemplates.psaApiNote: PSA's free public API (api.psacard.com, OAuth2 password grant with a free PSA account, 100 calls/day) exposes ONLY cert verification — GET /publicapi/cert/GetByCertNumber/{certNumber} — there is NO population endpoint; the psacard.com/pop report is not mirrored in the API. For programmatic pop, use PokemonPriceTracker's API (GET /api/psa/population/{cardId}, BYOK bearer key, ~100 credits/day free; their published pricing is inconsistent across pages — verify on signup) or PokeData.io Pro (paid). Both psacard.com/pop and gemrate.com 403 plain server fetches — deep-link the user out or use a headless browser. The ?q= deep-link on PSA pop search is best-effort/undocumented (est.); the reliable fallback is opening https://www.psacard.com/pop/search directly.
